# Handoff: project state as of Nov 21, 2026

Read this first in a new chat, then `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/BACKLOG.md` and `docs/IDEAS.md`. It records everything
decided and built across the long build session, so no context is lost.

## Where things stand
- **Branch:** `claude/file-editing-offline-9q9lv2` holds all work. PR #1 (everything up to the 3D campus) was merged
  into `main`. Everything after it is on the branch only, and needs a **new PR** to reach `main` (Vercel deploys from
  `main`). That covers the polish passes, the explored campus, day/night models, onboarding, the legend and these docs.
- **Ryan's laptop changes are not on GitHub yet.** Suggested flow: push them to a `laptop-work` branch, then merge it
  with this branch and resolve conflicts. Both branches touch the UI.
- **Backlog:** every item is done. The remaining work is the **UI polish plan** in `docs/BACKLOG.md` (typography,
  motion, accessibility, cover art) and the ideas awaiting approval in `docs/IDEAS.md` (§0 ranks them by hackathon win odds).

## What's built (one spec per feature in `specs/`)
| Spec | Feature |
|---|---|
| 001–009 | Foundation, missions/profiles, friends + building cards, replay, rank + badges, neighbourhoods, ping log, leaderboards, time-of-day lighting |
| 010 | The Goose quest-giver: original SVG portrait; Gemini re-voices briefings with a fact guard |
| 011 | Geo-pinned tags: server gate on revealed cells; upvotes give +10 Rep; local/demo mode |
| 012 | 11 sourced London landmark missions, map-menu overview, region tap raise, cinematic intro, brand emblem |
| 013 | Forest FM radio: facts-only scripts, Gemini TTS or the browser's speech voice, captions |
| 014 | Graduation Wrapped: story slides, fog timelapse, real stats, share card |
| 015 | Live LTC buses (GTFS + GTFS-RT), next arrivals, ride detection, Every Route badge |
| 016 | Faculty turf + 3-player heists |
| 017 | Polish pack: collectibles, radar, posters, fog decay, weather, student-written missions |
| 018 | Class Run: private schedule, next-class waypoints, on-time Rep |
| 019 | Hand-built 3D campus models (glTF via script) |
| 020 | Mustang City always explored inside Western's real boundary, sharp border, all 160 campus buildings modelled |

UI polish passes (commits after 019) changed the following:
- **Look:** soft rounded glass with no cut corners, sunset pill buttons, and the golden-hour palette.
- **Fog:** Chaikin-smoothed edges with a feathered rim.
- **Map:** one control stack, building framing on tap, and a postcard loading screen built from renders of our own campus.
- **Models and art:** day/night model variants and the soft Wrapped art.
- **New players:** onboarding cards and a map legend with layer toggles.

## Decisions to keep
- **Original IP only:** no GTA/Rockstar names, logos, fonts or art. Public copy may only say "GTA 6-inspired". No parody
  of the GTA logo; the cover-art collage uses our own wordmark (`docs/COVER_ART.md`).
- **Accuracy rule:** landmark, collectible and radio facts come from stored, sourced text. Gemini may restyle text but
  never adds facts, and numbers are guard-checked.
- **Mustang City cells** are always revealed but never count toward Rep, % explored, districts, leaderboards or sync.
- **Fog decay** is a haze only: explored ground never un-explores.
- **Privacy:** no live location sharing; the Class Run schedule stays on the device; loot challenges (an idea, not built)
  must be opt-in with coarse areas only.
- **Database:** keep Tiger Data (TimescaleDB hypertable + continuous aggregate, MLH prize). Supabase is recommended as
  an add-on for Realtime and Storage only, because Supabase dropped TimescaleDB on Postgres 17 (`docs/SETUP_KEYS.md`).
- **Turf** uses cleared cells per faculty, not Rep, because cells are what's geographic.
- **Design direction:** a clean, soft, premium mobile app. GTA 6 flavour comes from the art direction (postcards, sunset
  palette, full-bleed loading art, establishing-shot captions), not from hard or polygonal shapes.
- Push only to the `claude/...` branch unless Ryan says otherwise. Force-push was blocked once, so merge instead.

## Needs from Ryan (also `docs/IDEAS.md` §7 and `docs/SETUP_KEYS.md`)
- **Keys:** `GEMINI_API_KEY`, the Auth0 settings and `DATABASE_URL`, then run `npm run db:schema && npm run db:seed`.
  The schema has new tables and columns since the last seed: `tag_votes`, `missions.created_at` and the heist index.
- **Deploy:** a new PR from this branch into `main`.
- **Optional:** comic-panel art and icon (prompts in `docs/COVER_ART.md`).
- **Checks on the deployed site:** live LTC buses (the realtime host reset connections from the cloud build machine)
  and Open-Meteo weather (it returned 429 to the cloud machine).

## Running locally
- `.env.local` needs `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_TOKEN` (a public `pk.` token; allow localhost in its URL restrictions).
  `LTC_FIXTURE=1` simulates buses in dev only.
- `npm run dev`. Press **D** for demo controls: walk campus, reveal here, light presets, weather, fog ageing, sample turf,
  demo heist crew, replay intro.
- **Regenerate data:**
  - `npm run gtfs:build <unzipped LTC GTFS dir>` → `lib/data/ltc.json`
  - `npm run models:extract <dir of Mapbox Streets z15 tiles>` → `scripts/models/campus-all.json`
  - `npm run models:build` → `public/models/*.glb` (night and `-day` variants) + `lib/data/campusModels.json`
- **Cloud sessions:** the `mustang-city` cloud environment allows `api.mapbox.com`, `events.mapbox.com`,
  `gtfs.ltconline.ca`, `www.londontransit.ca` and `api.open-meteo.com`.

## Gotchas learned the hard way
- **Mapbox glTF:** vertex buffers must not be interleaved (`VertexLayout.SEPARATE`), indices must be uint16, and
  `addModel` needs absolute URLs. Axes: +X east, +Y up, +Z south. A `clip` layer needs `clip-layer-scope: ["basemap"]`,
  or it hides our own models whose anchor sits inside the clip polygon.
- **Material glow** ignores the layer's `model-emissive-strength`. That's why there are separate `-day` model files.
- **Next 16 with `cacheComponents`:** a route handler that doesn't read the request gets prerendered. Call `await connection()`.
- **The dev server sometimes serves stale CSS** after edits in this container. Restart `next dev` if styles don't change.
- **Tile-split buildings:** Mapbox vector tiles split buildings at tile edges. Footprint matching must test vertex
  overlap both ways (see `replacedByModel` in `MapView.tsx`).
- **Headless browser screenshots:** use `--use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader`. Run the scripts from the scratchpad,
  not the repo root, or the screenshots land in git.

## Ideas logged but not built (see `docs/IDEAS.md`)
- **Ranked list (§0):** Devpost trailer, comic-panel cover intro, live big-screen mirror, "wanted level" stars, The Goose
  calls you, the stash and carry inventory (Mustang City as the stash), loot challenges as a London trivia duel, pause
  music, photo mode and more.
- **3D models (§3):** phone photogrammetry is the upgrade path to photo-real facades.
- **Pause music (§4):** procedural, licensed or AI-generated routes.

# Mustang City — pitch & demo script

> **One line:** Most Western students spend four years in London and leave knowing only campus, Richmond Row and the 2 bus.
> Mustang City turns London into an open world you uncover — so you graduate knowing your city, and leave with memories of it.

## The story (say it like this)

1. **The problem (personal):** "Most of us didn't grow up here. We arrive at 18, live inside a bubble — campus, Richmond Row,
   one bus route — and four years later we leave. *Almost 85% of Western students leave London after they graduate.*\*
   Most will never come back. We spend four years in a city and never actually meet it."
2. **The insight:** "We already explore cities obsessively — in games. Open-world games make you *want* to see what's behind
   the fog. So what if London *was* the open world?"
3. **The product:** "Mustang City covers London in black fog. It only clears where you've physically walked. Western is your
   home base — Mustang City — and everything else is Forest State, waiting."
4. **Why you'd go:** "The Goose — our crime-boss quest-giver — sends you on missions to real places with real history:
   the house where insulin was conceived, the street that played 1980s New York for Apple TV. A photo proves you went;
   Gemini checks it. You earn Rep, unlock neighbourhoods, ride real LTC buses, and pull heists with people you just met."
5. **What you leave with:** "At graduation you get your Wrapped: the fog you cleared in the order you cleared it, the places,
   the photos, the people. Not just a degree — a map of your four years in London."
6. **Close:** "Graduate knowing your city."

\* Quote from Amir Farahi (London Institute) via 106.9 The X — **verify the exact figure before saying it on stage**; if unsure,
say "the vast majority". International students are ~24% of Western (Times Higher Education).

## Wow features — in priority order

Rank = (how much a judge notices it) × (how reliably it works on stage). Build/practice in this order.

| # | Moment | Why it lands | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Cinematic intro flight** (title card → letterboxed dive from Forest State into Mustang City) | First 15 seconds; instantly reads as "open-world game" | ✅ built |
| 2 | **Fog clearing timelapse** (Replay of a real walk at 16–48×) | The one image that explains the product | ✅ built — **record your real Saturday walk** |
| 3 | **3D Mustang City** (hand-built Middlesex tower, UC, 160 campus buildings, tap → history card) | Craft + "this is our campus" | ✅ built |
| 4 | **Mission → Gemini photo check → MISSION PASSED** | The game loop + sponsor tech in one beat | ⚠️ needs `GEMINI_API_KEY` (check-in missions work now) |
| 5 | **Live LTC buses** on the map + "Route 2 in 4 min" on a mission card | Real-time data; judges love "that's live" | ✅ working (114 live buses) |
| 6 | **Wrapped share card** — "Graduate knowing your city" | Emotional close: the memory you leave with | ✅ built |
| 7 | Neighbourhood unlock + "Entering East London" banner | Shows the city opening up | ✅ built |
| 8 | Crew compare + faculty turf + heist | Social pitch: meeting people | ✅ built — real accounts need Auth0 + DB |
| 9 | Forest FM radio host | Personality; Gemini TTS voice | ✅ built — Gemini voice needs key |
| 10 | Geo-pinned tags ("left by whoever came before you") | Memories left *for* others | ✅ built |

**Highest-leverage things still to do before judging:** (1) add the Gemini key and test a photo mission end to end,
(2) record one real campus walk for Replay, (3) drop in the cover art, (4) rehearse the script below 3×.

## Demo scripts

Use the **laptop phone frame** (judges see exactly the phone UI). Press **D** for the hidden demo panel. Have the iPhone
(home-screen icon) as backup and a recorded video as the last resort.

### 60 seconds (expo table / fly-by)
1. (0–10 s) Title card → **Tap to enter** → intro flight. *"Most Western students leave London never having seen it."*
2. (10–25 s) Demo panel → **Replay sample walk (48×)** — fog clears across campus. *"The fog only clears where you've walked."*
3. (25–40 s) Tap Middlesex College → history card. *"Every building has a story."*
4. (40–60 s) Profile → **Forest State Wrapped** → share card. *"Graduate knowing your city."*

### 3 minutes (main judging)
| Time | Beat | Do | Say |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:20 | Hook | Title card on screen | Story points 1–2 |
| 0:20–0:40 | Intro | Tap to enter → flight | "London becomes Forest State. Western is Mustang City — home base." |
| 0:40–1:05 | Fog | Demo panel → Replay your real walk (16×), then zoom out to city view | "Black fog everywhere you haven't been. % explored, neighbourhoods unlock at 30%." |
| 1:05–1:25 | 3D campus | Fly to Mustang City, tilt, tap Middlesex | "Hand-built 3D campus. Tap any building for its real history." |
| 1:25–2:05 | Mission | Missions → Banting House (or Meet The Family) → Goose briefing → Teleport (demo) → photo → **MISSION PASSED** | "The Goose sends you to real places. Gemini checks your photo. You earn Rep." |
| 2:05–2:25 | Live city | Zoom to downtown: live buses; open a mission card: "Route 2 in 4 min" | "That's live London Transit — missions tell you which bus gets you there." |
| 2:25–2:45 | Social | Crew → compare with a friend, show their fog; mention turf + heists | "Faculties fight over neighbourhoods. Heists need three people at once — strangers meet." |
| 2:45–3:00 | Close | Profile → Wrapped → share card | Story points 5–6: "Graduate knowing your city." |

### 5 minutes (if you get it)
Add after 2:45: Forest FM radio segment (15 s) · leave a tag (20 s) · "Entering East London" banner via demo walk (Old East Village is inside it) (20 s) ·
tech slide: Next.js PWA, Mapbox Standard + hand-built glTF, H3 fog, Gemini (vision + TTS + guarded rewrites),
Auth0 @uwo.ca Action, Tiger Data hypertable + continuous aggregate, live GTFS-RT (45 s).

## Before you walk up (checklist)
- [ ] Laptop: app open, intro **not yet seen this session** (so the flight plays), demo panel tested, light preset = Dusk
- [ ] Sound on (MISSION PASSED sting, radio) — but low
- [ ] Phone: home-screen icon, logged in, location on, battery > 50%
- [ ] Real Replay walk recorded; a real mission photo on the laptop for the photo picker
- [ ] Projector check: text readable at the frame's scaled size
- [ ] Backup video on the desktop

## Likely questions (additions to the brief's Q&A)
- **"Why would students keep using it after week one?"** Fog slowly hazes over (come back), weekly turf, new student missions,
  Class Run turns your daily commute into Rep, and Wrapped rewards the whole four years.
- **"What about students who never leave campus?"** Missions start at the campus edge and use buses — the app literally tells
  you which bus to take next.
- **"Does the city benefit?"** Students who know the city are more likely to stay after graduation; local businesses can sponsor missions.
- **"Is location safe?"** No live location sharing. Friends only see *where* you've been (cleared fog), never *when* or where you are.

Sources: [106.9 The X (London Institute quote)](https://www.1069thex.com/?p=24964) ·
[Times Higher Education — Western](https://resouces-cms.prd.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/western-university)
# Mustang City — Product Brief

Hack Western 13 · Nov 20, 2026 · @Ryan

## Summary

Mustang City is a mobile web app (PWA) that turns London, Ontario into **Forest State**, a GTA 6-inspired open-world map covered in black fog. # Mustang City — pitch & demo script

> **One line:** Most Western students spend four years in London and leave knowing only campus, Richmond Row and the 2 bus.
> Mustang City turns London into an open world you uncover — so you graduate knowing your city, and leave with memories of it.

## The story (say it like this)

1. **The problem (personal):** "Most of us didn't grow up here. We arrive at 18, live inside a bubble — campus, Richmond Row,
   one bus route — and four years later we leave. *Almost 85% of Western students leave London after they graduate.*\*
   Most will never come back. We spend four years in a city and never actually meet it."
2. **The insight:** "We already explore cities obsessively — in games. Open-world games make you *want* to see what's behind
   the fog. So what if London *was* the open world?"
3. **The product:** "Mustang City covers London in black fog. It only clears where you've physically walked. Western is your
   home base — Mustang City — and everything else is Forest State, waiting."
4. **Why you'd go:** "The Goose — our crime-boss quest-giver — sends you on missions to real places with real history:
   the house where insulin was conceived, the street that played 1980s New York for Apple TV. A photo proves you went;
   Gemini checks it. You earn Rep, unlock neighbourhoods, ride real LTC buses, and pull heists with people you just met."
5. **What you leave with:** "At graduation you get your Wrapped: the fog you cleared in the order you cleared it, the places,
   the photos, the people. Not just a degree — a map of your four years in London."
6. **Close:** "Graduate knowing your city."

\* Quote from Amir Farahi (London Institute) via 106.9 The X — **verify the exact figure before saying it on stage**; if unsure,
say "the vast majority". International students are ~24% of Western (Times Higher Education).

## Wow features — in priority order

Rank = (how much a judge notices it) × (how reliably it works on stage). Build/practice in this order.

| # | Moment | Why it lands | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Cinematic intro flight** (title card → letterboxed dive from Forest State into Mustang City) | First 15 seconds; instantly reads as "open-world game" | ✅ built |
| 2 | **Fog clearing timelapse** (Replay of a real walk at 16–48×) | The one image that explains the product | ✅ built — **record your real Saturday walk** |
| 3 | **3D Mustang City** (hand-built Middlesex tower, UC, 160 campus buildings, tap → history card) | Craft + "this is our campus" | ✅ built |
| 4 | **Mission → Gemini photo check → MISSION PASSED** | The game loop + sponsor tech in one beat | ⚠️ needs `GEMINI_API_KEY` (check-in missions work now) |
| 5 | **Live LTC buses** on the map + "Route 2 in 4 min" on a mission card | Real-time data; judges love "that's live" | ✅ working (114 live buses) |
| 6 | **Wrapped share card** — "Graduate knowing your city" | Emotional close: the memory you leave with | ✅ built |
| 7 | Neighbourhood unlock + "Entering East London" banner | Shows the city opening up | ✅ built |
| 8 | Crew compare + faculty turf + heist | Social pitch: meeting people | ✅ built — real accounts need Auth0 + DB |
| 9 | Forest FM radio host | Personality; Gemini TTS voice | ✅ built — Gemini voice needs key |
| 10 | Geo-pinned tags ("left by whoever came before you") | Memories left *for* others | ✅ built |

**Highest-leverage things still to do before judging:** (1) add the Gemini key and test a photo mission end to end,
(2) record one real campus walk for Replay, (3) drop in the cover art, (4) rehearse the script below 3×.

## Demo scripts

Use the **laptop phone frame** (judges see exactly the phone UI). Press **D** for the hidden demo panel. Have the iPhone
(home-screen icon) as backup and a recorded video as the last resort.

### 60 seconds (expo table / fly-by)
1. (0–10 s) Title card → **Tap to enter** → intro flight. *"Most Western students leave London never having seen it."*
2. (10–25 s) Demo panel → **Replay sample walk (48×)** — fog clears across campus. *"The fog only clears where you've walked."*
3. (25–40 s) Tap Middlesex College → history card. *"Every building has a story."*
4. (40–60 s) Profile → **Forest State Wrapped** → share card. *"Graduate knowing your city."*

### 3 minutes (main judging)
| Time | Beat | Do | Say |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:20 | Hook | Title card on screen | Story points 1–2 |
| 0:20–0:40 | Intro | Tap to enter → flight | "London becomes Forest State. Western is Mustang City — home base." |
| 0:40–1:05 | Fog | Demo panel → Replay your real walk (16×), then zoom out to city view | "Black fog everywhere you haven't been. % explored, neighbourhoods unlock at 30%." |
| 1:05–1:25 | 3D campus | Fly to Mustang City, tilt, tap Middlesex | "Hand-built 3D campus. Tap any building for its real history." |
| 1:25–2:05 | Mission | Missions → Banting House (or Meet The Family) → Goose briefing → Teleport (demo) → photo → **MISSION PASSED** | "The Goose sends you to real places. Gemini checks your photo. You earn Rep." |
| 2:05–2:25 | Live city | Zoom to downtown: live buses; open a mission card: "Route 2 in 4 min" | "That's live London Transit — missions tell you which bus gets you there." |
| 2:25–2:45 | Social | Crew → compare with a friend, show their fog; mention turf + heists | "Faculties fight over neighbourhoods. Heists need three people at once — strangers meet." |
| 2:45–3:00 | Close | Profile → Wrapped → share card | Story points 5–6: "Graduate knowing your city." |

### 5 minutes (if you get it)
Add after 2:45: Forest FM radio segment (15 s) · leave a tag (20 s) · "Entering East London" banner via demo walk (Old East Village is inside it) (20 s) ·
tech slide: Next.js PWA, Mapbox Standard + hand-built glTF, H3 fog, Gemini (vision + TTS + guarded rewrites),
Auth0 @uwo.ca Action, Tiger Data hypertable + continuous aggregate, live GTFS-RT (45 s).

## Before you walk up (checklist)
- [ ] Laptop: app open, intro **not yet seen this session** (so the flight plays), demo panel tested, light preset = Dusk
- [ ] Sound on (MISSION PASSED sting, radio) — but low
- [ ] Phone: home-screen icon, logged in, location on, battery > 50%
- [ ] Real Replay walk recorded; a real mission photo on the laptop for the photo picker
- [ ] Projector check: text readable at the frame's scaled size
- [ ] Backup video on the desktop

## Likely questions (additions to the brief's Q&A)
- **"Why would students keep using it after week one?"** Fog slowly hazes over (come back), weekly turf, new student missions,
  Class Run turns your daily commute into Rep, and Wrapped rewards the whole four years.
- **"What about students who never leave campus?"** Missions start at the campus edge and use buses — the app literally tells
  you which bus to take next.
- **"Does the city benefit?"** Students who know the city are more likely to stay after graduation; local businesses can sponsor missions.
- **"Is location safe?"** No live location sharing. Friends only see *where* you've been (cleared fog), never *when* or where you are.

Here's everything for the Devpost form. I pulled it from your handoff, pitch and brief docs, and there are no em dashes in any of it.

---

## About the project (paste into Project Story)

```markdown
## Inspiration

Most of us didn't grow up in London. We arrive at 18, live inside a bubble of campus, Richmond Row and one bus route, and four years later the vast majority of us leave. We spend four years in a city and never actually meet it.

We already explore cities obsessively, just in games. Open-world games make you *want* to see what's behind the fog. So I asked: what if London was the open world?

## What it does

**Mustang City** is a GTA 6-inspired mobile web app that turns London, Ontario into **Forest State**, an open-world map covered in black fog. The fog only clears where you've physically walked. Western's campus is your home base, Mustang City, and everything else is waiting to be uncovered.

- **Fog of war:** your real GPS path clears the map, cell by cell, with smoothed, feathered edges.
- **3D Mustang City:** all 160 campus buildings are modelled in 3D, with day and night versions. Tap any building for its real history.
- **Photo missions:** The Goose, an original crime-boss quest-giver, sends you to real places with real history, like the house where insulin was conceived. Snap a photo to prove you went, and Gemini checks it. Then: **MISSION PASSED**.
- **Rep, ranks and neighbourhoods:** earn Rep, unlock badges, and watch "Entering Old East Village" banners as the city opens up.
- **Live LTC buses:** real-time buses on the map, plus "Route 2 in 4 min" right on your mission card. The app detects bus rides too.
- **Social:** compare fog with friends, fight for neighbourhoods by faculty, and pull three-player heists that get strangers to meet.
- **Forest FM:** an in-game radio host that reads facts-only scripts in a Gemini TTS voice.
- **Geo-pinned tags:** leave notes on places for whoever comes after you.
- **Class Run:** your daily walk to class earns Rep for being on time. Your schedule never leaves your phone.
- **Graduation Wrapped:** a story-style recap of the fog you cleared, in the order you cleared it, with the places and the people. Not just a degree, but a map of your four years in London.

**Graduate knowing your city.**

## How I built it

- **Frontend:** Next.js (App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind v4 and Motion, shipped as a PWA for the iPhone home screen. On a laptop it renders inside a phone frame.
- **Map:** one Mapbox GL JS instance on the Standard style. The fog is an H3 hex grid merged into a single polygon and smoothed with Chaikin's algorithm.
- **3D campus:** I wrote a script that turns building footprints into glTF models, with separate day and night files because Mapbox ignores emissive strength on material glow.
- **AI:** Gemini handles photo verification, mission briefings in The Goose's voice, and radio TTS. A strict rule covers all of it: facts come from stored, sourced text. Gemini may restyle a sentence but never add a fact, and a guard checks every number.
- **Transit:** LTC's static GTFS is preprocessed into a compact dataset, and the live bus positions and arrivals come from GTFS-Realtime.
- **Auth and data:** Auth0 with a post-login Action that only allows @uwo.ca accounts. Data lives in Tiger Data (Postgres + TimescaleDB): location pings go into a hypertable with a continuous aggregate for leaderboards.
- **Hosting:** Vercel. Weather comes from Open-Meteo.
- **Process:** I built this solo with AI coding agents, writing a spec for each of 20 features before building it.

## Challenges

- **Getting custom 3D models into Mapbox:** I found out the hard way that vertex buffers can't be interleaved, indices must be uint16, and model URLs must be absolute. Clip layers also hid my own models until I scoped them to the basemap.
- **Buildings split at tile edges:** Mapbox vector tiles cut buildings at tile boundaries, so matching footprints to my models meant testing vertex overlap both ways.
- **Fog that looks good:** raw hexagons look like a spreadsheet. Merging, smoothing and feathering them took several passes.
- **Live transit from the cloud:** the LTC realtime server reset TLS connections from the build machine, so I added an HTTP fallback.
- **Accuracy vs. personality:** I wanted The Goose to be funny without making up history. That's why the fact guard exists.
- **Privacy:** there's no live location sharing. Friends only see *where* you've been (cleared fog), never *when*, and never where you are right now.

## What I learned

- How to bend a map engine into a game engine: fog, a HUD, mission flow and a cinematic intro camera.
- How to generate 3D glTF from scratch, and how to work with GTFS and GTFS-Realtime.
- How to design around time-series data with TimescaleDB hypertables.
- How to keep an LLM useful without letting it make things up.
- How to scope ruthlessly as a solo builder: one strong image (fog clearing as you walk) beats ten half-finished features.

## What's next

Phone photogrammetry for photo-real campus facades, student-written missions at scale, and local businesses sponsoring missions to get students off campus and into the city.
```

---

## Built with (25 tags, the maximum)

```
next.js, typescript, react, tailwind-css, motion, mapbox, mapbox-gl-js, h3, gltf, auth0, tiger-data, timescaledb, postgresql, gemini, google-gemini, gtfs, gtfs-realtime, open-meteo, vercel, pwa, node.js, javascript, web-speech-api, claude-code, spec-kit
```

---

## "Try it out" links

- **Code:** https://github.com/RyanPeters06/mustang-city
- **Live app:** your Vercel URL (I don't have it, so add it yourself)

---

A few things to check before you submit:
- **Make the repo public** if it's private, or the Code link won't work for judges.
- **Photo missions say Gemini checks the photo.** That only works once `GEMINI_API_KEY` is set on Vercel, and the handoff says it hasn't been tested end to end yet. If you don't get to it, soften that line.
- **Heists, the faculty turf fight and comparing fog with friends** need real accounts, so Auth0 and the database have to be live on the deployed site.
- **Adjust "20 features"** if your count of specs is different.
